w10_P4_000203: A conveyor drive is tuned on a factory test bed, and the rate at which its acceleration builds, in metres per second cubed, follows 1t^2 + 4t. Between t = 3 seconds and t = 4 seconds the acceleration accumulates from zero at the start of that interval, and the value reached at the end is the bench's base figure. The tuning sheet then doubles that base figure by 2 for the twin drive, subtracts a slip allowance of 29, subtracts a gearbox allowance of 24, and finally adds a torque contribution of 19, giving the acceleration in metres per second squared that the drive actually delivers. The conveyor pushes a crate of 86000 grams at exactly that acceleration. What force, in newtons, does the drive apply to the crate?
w10_P4_000207: A launch bench brings a carriage of 24000 grams up to speed, and the carriage's acceleration in metres per second squared follows 2t^2 + 2t, with t the time in seconds. Between t = 3 seconds and t = 4 seconds the speed builds from rest at the start of that interval, and the speed reached at the end is the launch speed. The logger records the energy the carriage carries because of its motion at that speed. Because 4 carriages go out per launch, 5 launches make a set, and 8 sets make the programme, the record is multiplied by 4, then by 5, then by 8. A fixed instrument offset of 28 J is added to the programme total. What is the programme total, in joules?
w10_P4_000218: A rolling mill drives a slab carrier of 153000 grams, and the rate at which its acceleration builds, in metres per second cubed, follows 5t^2 + 1t. Between t = 1 second and t = 3 seconds the acceleration accumulates from zero at the start of that interval, and the value reached at the end is the acceleration the mill uses. The control system works out the force needed to drive the carrier at that acceleration and expresses it in kilonewtons. It then subtracts a contractual credit of 30 kN, adds a rigging allowance of 9 kN, and adds a further handling allowance of 8 kN. The mill's roller table is 15 m long, a dimension the control system never uses. What figure, in kilonewtons, does the control system report?
w10_P4_000222: A shunting locomotive pushes a wagon of 117 kg on a test rig, and the rate at which the wagon's acceleration builds, in metres per second cubed, follows 2t^2 + 3t. Between t = 0 seconds and t = 2 seconds the acceleration accumulates from zero, and the value reached at t = 2 seconds is the one used. From the force needed to drive the wagon at that acceleration the software subtracts a coupling tare of 27 N, then expresses the remainder in kilonewtons. That converted figure is multiplied by 8 for the 8 wagons in the rake, and a fixed contractual allowance of 20 kN is added at the end. The rig's siding is 40 m long, which plays no part in the calculation. What number, in kilonewtons, does the software report?
w10_P4_000226: A calibration bench carries 8 identical reference masses, and the routine works through every distinct group of 4 that can be chosen from them. The number of such groups is, in metres per second squared, the acceleration the bench applies to a shuttle of 37 kg. The controller records the force needed to drive the shuttle and multiplies it by 3, since the routine is run on 3 axes. It expresses that total in kilonewtons and then subtracts a frame tare of 1 kN. The bench is 2 m wide, a dimension the controller records but never uses. What number, in kilonewtons, does the controller report?
w10_P4_000228: A stores clerk counts 303 items in one bin and 356 in another, and works out the largest whole number that divides both counts exactly with nothing left over. A test slider of 11000 grams is released along a level bench at a speed, in metres per second, equal to that number. The bench software records the energy the slider carries because of its motion, then subtracts a friction allowance of 3 J, a bearing allowance of 16 J, and an air-drag allowance of 17 J in turn. Finally it adds a standing calibration offset of 9 J. What number, in joules, does the software report?
w10_P4_000231: A workshop's closing entry is 9 N less than a figure that was itself 29 N more than a rig total. The rig total is 5 times a single-station value, since 5 stations run together, and each single-station value is what you get by adding a bearing preload of 27 N to the force needed for one push. Each push accelerates a carriage of 198000 grams, and the acceleration in metres per second squared is the number of distinct pairs that can be chosen from the workshop's 13 test masses. What number, in newtons, is the closing entry?
w10_P4_000238: A test-house certificate carries a number found by adding a rigging allowance of 19 kN to a converted reading. That converted reading is the kilonewton form of the force needed to accelerate a sled of 72 kg along the house's rail. The acceleration used, in metres per second squared, is what remains when 26 is subtracted from the total of the squares of the whole numbers from 1 to 5. What number, in kilonewtons, appears on the certificate?
w10_P4_000239: A quarry conveyor accelerates a rock tray of 166 kg along its frame. The acceleration in metres per second squared is found by taking the larger of the two values of x for which x^2 - 3x + 2 = 0 and adding a drive contribution of 8 to it. The control system records the force needed to move the tray and multiplies it by 7, because 7 trays travel together. It then multiplies that total by 9 for the 9 conveyors in the quarry. The conveyor frame is 25 m long, a length the control system never uses. What figure, in newtons, does the control system report?
w10_P4_000241: An engineer fits the curve 2x^3 - 5x^2 to a test trace, with x the elapsed time in seconds. The rate at which that fitted curve is changing at the instant x = 3 seconds gives a base figure, and adding a drive contribution of 15 to it gives the speed, in metres per second, of a carrier of 26 kg. The bench records the energy the carrier holds because of its motion at that speed, and a fixed instrument offset of 12 J is added to the record. The result is then expressed in kilojoules. The bench rail is 4 m long, a dimension that plays no part. What value, in kilojoules, does the bench report?
w10_P4_000244: A hoist accelerates a load of 139000 grams, and the acceleration in metres per second squared is 9 times the sum of 3 and 2. The control system works out the force needed to drive the load and expresses it in kilonewtons. From that converted figure it subtracts a frame tare of 2 kN, then a contractual credit of 20 kN, and finally adds a rigging allowance of 1 kN. What number, in kilonewtons, does the control system report?
w10_P4_000245: A test facility publishes a figure that is 2 times a paired total, because the runs are paired. Each paired total is itself 2 times a converted single-run reading, since two carriages run together. That converted reading is the kilojoule form of the energy a carriage of 54 kg carries because of its motion. The carriage's speed in metres per second is the rate at which its fitted position curve 5x^3 - 5x^2 is changing at the instant x = 2 seconds, with x the time in seconds and the position in metres. What figure, in kilojoules, does the facility publish?
w10_P4_000249: A machine shop fits the curve 3x^3 - 2x^2 to the recorded position, in metres, of a tool slide, with x the time in seconds. At the instant x = 3 seconds the rate at which the slope of that fitted curve is itself changing gives a base figure, and adding a drive contribution of 4 to it gives the acceleration, in metres per second squared, applied to a tool head of 21 kg. The controller records the force needed for that acceleration and multiplies it by 10, since 10 heads are driven together. It multiplies the result by 8 for the 8 slides on the machine, and then by 9 for the 9 machines in the shop. What figure, in newtons, does the controller report for the shop?
w10_P4_000259: A plant report closes with a number that is 28 N more than a site total. The site total is 8 times a line figure, and the line figure is 5 times a station value, since 8 lines and 5 stations are involved. Each station value is what you get by adding a bearing preload of 23 N to the force needed to accelerate a carrier of 29 kg. The acceleration in metres per second squared is the number of distinct pairs that can be chosen from the plant's 6 test masses. The report also notes that the plant floor is 50 m long, which never enters the calculation. What number, in newtons, closes the report?
w10_P4_000265: A teaching laboratory has 18 red weights and 101 blue weights, and the demonstrator works out the largest whole number that divides both counts exactly with nothing left over. A glider of 27000 grams is then released along the air track at a speed, in metres per second, equal to that number. The bench records the energy the glider carries because of its motion and multiplies it by 9, because 9 identical releases are made. The total is expressed in kilojoules, and a fixed instrument allowance of 22 kJ is added. The track is 2 m long, a dimension the bench never uses. What value, in kilojoules, does the bench report?
w10_P4_000268: A workshop counts 150 bolts in one tray and 55 in another, and the foreman works out the largest whole number that divides both counts exactly with nothing left over. A test carrier of 55000 grams is launched along the rail at a speed, in metres per second, equal to that number. The bench records the energy the carrier holds because of its motion and adds a fixed instrument offset of 24 J to the record. That sum is multiplied by 12, because the programme calls for 12 identical launches, and the total is expressed in kilojoules. The rail sits 1.5 m above the floor, a height the bench never uses. What total, in kilojoules, does the bench report?
w10_P4_000274: A press line drives a tool of 29 kg, and the rate at which its acceleration builds, in metres per second cubed, follows 3t^2 + 8t. Between t = 1 second and t = 3 seconds the acceleration accumulates from zero at the start of that interval, and the value reached at the end is the acceleration used. To the force needed to drive the tool at that acceleration the controller adds a die preload of 22 N. It multiplies the sum by 8 for the 8 tools on a press, by 11 for the 11 presses on the line, and by 10 for the 10 lines in the plant. The line's guard rail is 30 m long, a figure the controller never uses. What total, in newtons, does the controller report?
w10_P4_000275: A depot has 18 pallets on one dock and 60 on another, and the supervisor works out the largest whole number that divides both counts exactly with nothing left over. That number is, in metres per second squared, the acceleration his tug applies to a load of 63000 grams. The control system records the force needed to move the load and expresses it in kilonewtons, then multiplies the converted figure by 11 for the 11 tugs in the depot and by 5 for the 5 working days in the week. A fixed rigging allowance of 17 kN is added at the end. Each dock door is 4 m wide, a dimension that plays no part. What number, in kilonewtons, does the control system report?
w10_P4_000281: A logger fits the curve 5x^3 - 2x^2 to a trace, with x the time in seconds. The rate at which that fitted curve is changing at the instant x = 1 second gives, in metres per second, the speed of a probe of 11 kg. The system records the energy the probe carries because of its motion and expresses it in kilojoules. From that converted value a contractual credit of 22 kJ is subtracted, and the remainder is multiplied by 8 because 8 probes fly the same profile. The launch tower is 20 m tall, a height that never enters the calculation. What number, in kilojoules, does the system report?
w10_P4_000286: A gantry report ends with a number that is 2 times an earlier total, because the hall has two identical gantries. That earlier total is 4 times a converted single-carriage reading, since each gantry carries 4 carriages. The converted reading is the kilonewton form of the force needed to accelerate one carriage of 58 kg along the beam, and the carriage's acceleration in metres per second squared is the rate at which its fitted position curve 1x^3 - 2x^2 is changing at the instant x = 2 seconds, with x the time in seconds and the position in metres. The beam spans 18 m, a length the report notes but does not use. What number, in kilonewtons, ends the report?
w10_P4_000289: A launcher brings a puck of 10000 grams up to speed along a level rail, and the puck's acceleration in metres per second squared follows 2t^2 + 6t between t = 0 seconds and t = 1 second, starting from rest. The energy the puck carries because of its motion at the end of that interval is recorded and expressed in kilojoules. Because 9 pucks are fired in a run, 4 runs make a session, and 5 sessions make the study, the converted figure is multiplied by 9, then by 4, then by 5. The rail is 6 m long, a dimension that never enters the energy account. What total, in kilojoules, does the study report?
w10_P4_000292: A test report ends with a number obtained by taking 1 N off a value that was itself 26 N more than a corrected reading, and that corrected reading was the raw force less a frame tare of 30 N. The raw force is the force needed to accelerate a slide of 173000 grams. The acceleration used is 4 times a base value in metres per second squared, and that base value is what the rate curve 1t^2 + 4t accumulates between t = 2 seconds and t = 3 seconds, starting from zero at t = 2 seconds and with t the time in seconds. What number, in newtons, ends the report?
w10_P4_000293: A haulage summary ends with a figure in kilonewtons, converted from a total that had a coupling tare of 22 N subtracted from it. That total was 6 times a rake figure, and the rake figure was 3 times the force needed to drive one wagon. Each wagon has a mass of 190000 grams, and its acceleration in metres per second squared is what the rate curve 1t^2 + 6t accumulates between t = 1 second and t = 2 seconds, starting from zero at t = 1 second and with t the time in seconds. What figure, in kilonewtons, ends the summary?
w10_P4_000295: A quarry report closes with a number that is 9 times a site figure, because 9 sites run the same plant. Each site figure is 5 times a converted single-machine reading, since 5 machines work at a site. The converted reading is the kilonewton form of the force needed to accelerate a crusher jaw of 99 kg, and the acceleration in metres per second squared is what the rate curve 3t^2 + 4t accumulates between t = 0 seconds and t = 3 seconds, starting from zero and with t the time in seconds. What number, in kilonewtons, closes the report?
w10_P4_000300: A vibration laboratory fits the curve 3x^3 - 3x^2 to a recorded trace, with x the time in seconds. At the instant x = 3 seconds the rate at which the slope of that fitted curve is itself changing gives, in metres per second, the speed of a test mass of 14 kg on the shaker. The bench records the energy the mass carries because of its motion, then subtracts a damping allowance of 25 J, a mounting allowance of 9 J, and finally adds a calibration offset of 3 J. The shaker head is 0.4 m across, a dimension the bench never uses. What number, in joules, does the bench report?
